intent_snapshot.goal: Implement the Kernel-side Batch Authorization defined by docs/specs/unattended-initiative-batch-run.spec.md section 3.2: one literal-user confirmation binds {batch_id, initiative_slug, plan_digest, branch, base_head, budget, actor_id, confirmation_ref, expires_at, nonce} into a per-child one-shot capability registry that derives a fresh per-child EnrollmentCapabilityBinding at enroll time, enforces plan membership, expiry, unused child slots, and an advancing Git HEAD lineage, and fails closed with zero Kernel writes on every rejected path.

acceptance.assertion: createBatchAuthorityRegistry issues a Batch Authorization only from a literal-user confirmation reference and validates every binding field by exact match, mirroring createEnrollmentAuthorityRegistry semantics. Issue requires actor_id 'user', a nonempty confirmation_ref, a nonempty nonce, expires_at strictly after now, a nonempty branch, a committed 40-hex base_head, and a plan_digest that is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the ordered children [{task_id,intent_path,intent_revision,intent_content_hash,blocked_by}]. Any missing, empty, mismatched, or reordered field is rejected before issuance. Unlike the single-use enrollment capability, the batch capability is consumed per child: consumeChild(capability, expected, task_id) marks exactly one child slot used and leaves the authorization valid for the remaining unused children until expires_at. Consuming a task_id absent from the confirmed plan, a task_id whose slot is already consumed, or any child after expires_at is rejected and consumes nothing. Rejected issue and consume paths leave the capability registry and all Kernel state bytes unchanged.

deriveChildEnrollment recomputes preparation for the named child through the existing preparePiCanary path at enroll time and never reuses a preparation_digest captured at batch confirmation, because enrollment rejects a moved Git HEAD and every settled child moves it. The derived EnrollmentCapabilityBinding carries the freshly recomputed preparation_digest together with the batch confirmation_ref and actor_id, and its intent_revision and intent_content_hash must equal the values recorded for that child in plan_digest; any divergence yields batch_child_intent_changed and performs no enrollment. Derivation additionally asserts the HEAD lineage invariant: preparation.git_base_head must equal the batch state expected_head, which starts at base_head and advances only to a commit created by this batch on its own branch; any other value yields batch_head_lineage_broken with zero writes. enrollCanaryTask accepts a batch-derived capability and consumes the batch child slot inside the same store lock as the TaskRecord write, so an interrupted enrollment never leaves a consumed slot without a TaskRecord or a TaskRecord without a consumed slot. Existing single-task enrollment behavior, its digest and HEAD checks, tombstone and workspace-claim rejections, and its byte-level failure atomicity are unchanged.

findings.summary: The atomicity failure-injection test in tests/kernel-batch-authority.test.ts ('leaves no consumed slot when the bound record write cannot commit') passes vacuously: it chmods .imm/state to 0o500 while .imm/state/locks does not yet exist (makeRoot creates only .imm/state, and preparePiCanary/readTaskRecordRaw/readWorkspaceStateRaw/readBackendClaim create no directories), so withKernelStoreLock -> ensureSecureDirectory's mkdirSync of .imm/state/locks throws EACCES before registry.consume and consumeChild ever execute, leaving the new releaseChild rollback try/catch in plugins/immune-brain/runtime/kernel/enrollment.ts with zero coverage and the bidirectional slot/TaskRecord guarantee unverified.

expected_head in deriveChildEnrollment and EnrollBatchContext is entirely caller-supplied and is never anchored to the confirmed binding's base_head (no assertion that a derivation with zero consumed slots uses base_head), so the literal-user-confirmed base_head constrains nothing and the lineage invariant reduces to a caller self-assertion.

Batch expiry fails open on an unparseable clock: enrollCanaryTask passes Date.parse(input.now) into consumeChild and deriveChildEnrollment passes Date.parse(input.now) into inspect, and a NaN makes 'Date.parse(state.expires_at) <= now' false, so an expired authorization is consumed; the pre-existing single-task path avoids this by defaulting to Date.now().
